grammar_textbook_based.topic: What do you like?

structures.title: Present simple
structures.content:
a. Affirmative
I / We / You wear casual clothes.
He / She / [It] watches films.
b. Negative
I / We / You / They don't study art.
He / She / [It] doesn't play rugby.
c. Questions and short answers
Do I / you / we / they live in a house?
Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Does he / she / [it] like to sing?
Yes, he / she / [it] does.
No, he / she / [it] doesn't.

structures.title: Present continuous
structures.content:
a. Affirmative
I'm dancing.
You / We / They're cooking.
He / She / [It]'s watching a DVD.
b. Negative
I'm not talking to Jane.
We / You / They aren't listening.
He / She / [It] isn't listening.
c. Questions and short answers
Am I going fast?
Yes, I am.
Are we / you / they eating?
Yes, we are.
Is / he / she / [it] playing the guitar?
No, he / she / [it] isn't.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Fact or fiction?

structures.title: Past simple
structures.content:
a. Affirmative
I read the book in class.
They enjoyed the autobiography.
b. Negative
I didn't see the film adaptation.
They didn't want to read the ending.
c. Questions
Did / finish the book?
Did you like the main character?
d. Short answers
Yes, I / you / he / she / it / we / they did.
No, I / you / he / she / it / we / they didn't.

structures.title: was / were
structures.content:
a. Affirmative
He was an actor.
Many events were free.
b. Negative
It wasn't a good performance.
They weren't in the show.
c. Questions
Was I / he / she / [it] an explorer?
Were we / you / they critical about the novel?
d. Short answers
No, I / he / she / [it] wasn't.
Yes, we / you / they were.

structures.title: could / couldn't
structures.content:
a. Affirmative
You could visit many places.
b. Negative
We couldn't see the stage.
c. Questions
Could they perform?
d. Short answers
Yes, they could. / No, they couldn't.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Wild weather

structures.title: Past continuous
structures.content:
a. Affirmative
I / He / She / [It] was talking with friends.
We / You / They were doing their homework.
b. Negative
I / He / She / [It] wasn't tidying her room.
We / You / They weren't eating lunch.
c. Questions
Was it snowing?
Were we / you / they walking?
d. Short answers
Yes, it was.
No, we / you / they weren't.

structures.title: Adjectives and Adverbs
structures.content:
It's cold. Dress warmly.
It's foggy. Drive carefully.
It's raining hard today.
I can easily do this exercise.
She speaks English well.

structures.title: Past continuous and past simple
structures.content:
His mum was cooking dinner when she heard a shout.
Lots of brick fell on me while I was lying on the ground.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Life on Earth

structures.title: Comparatives and superlatives
structures.content:
faster - the fastest
hotter - the hottest
funnier - the funniest
more expensive - the most expensive
better - the best
worse - the worst

structures.title: a / an, some, any, countable nouns
structures.content:
Countable nouns
He climbed a mountain.
There's an elephant.
There are some great beaches.
I haven't got a car.
There aren't any animals on the island.
Is that a waterfall?
Are there any owls?

Uncountable nouns
I need some information about volunteering.
There isn't any clean water in some countries.
Did you try any special food?

structures.title: Much, many, a lot of
structures.content:
Countable nouns
There are a lot of volunteering projects.
I didn't go to many boring places.
How many people were there?

Uncountable nouns
We had a lot of time to explore the city.
There isn't much rain in summer.
How much food will we need?

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Let's experiment

structures.title: will / won't
structures.content:
a. Affirmative
Robots will work for humans.
We will be able to do more things we enjoy.
b. Negative
Learning a second language won't be necessary.
c. Questions
Will humans be able to fly?
d. Short answers
Yes, they will. / No, they won't.

structures.title: First conditional
structures.content:
a. Situation – result
If scientists continue to experiment, we will find cures for more diseases.
b. Result – situation
There will be more explosions in our science class if we aren't careful with the chemicals.

structures.title: be going to
structures.content: a. affirmative: I'm going to buy a magazine with my pocket money. b. negative: We aren't going to go on holiday this year. c. questions: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.

structures.content: I'll see you tomorrow / next week / this summer / soon. When I go on holiday, I'll buy some souvenirs.

structures.title: would like

structures.title: Present perfect
structures.content: a. affirmative: I've seen lots of monuments. He / She / [It]'s visited interesting places. structures.content: present simple, present continuous, past simple, past continuous, present perfect, will, be going to

structures.content: a. affirmative: You should go to the doctor if you feel ill. b. negative: You shouldn't forget to eat fruit and vegetables. c. questions: Should you tell an adult? d. short answers: Yes, you should. / No, you shouldn't.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Present perfect simple (with for and since)

structures.title: Present perfect simple (with for and since)
structures.content: This structure is used to talk about actions that started in the past and continue to the present. 'For' is used for periods of time, and 'since' is used for points in time.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Present perfect simple vs. past simple

structures.title: Present perfect simple vs. past simple
structures.content: The present perfect tense is used for actions that have a connection to the present. The past simple tense is used for actions that happened at a specific time in the past.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Articles (a, an, the or no article)

structures.title: Articles (a, an, the or no article)
structures.content: Articles are used before nouns. 'A' and 'an' are indefinite articles, 'the' is a definite article, and sometimes no article is used.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Adverbs of manner and comparison

structures.title: Adverbs of manner and comparison
structures.content: Adverbs of manner describe how something is done. Adverbs of comparison are used to compare two things.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Indefinite pronouns (everyone, no one, someone, etc.)

structures.title: Indefinite pronouns (everyone, no one, someone, etc.)
structures.content: Indefinite pronouns refer to people or things without specifying which ones.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Present perfect continuous

structures.title: Present perfect continuous
structures.content: This structure is used to talk about actions that started in the past and continue to the present, often with a result in the present.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Present perfect continuous vs. present perfect simple

structures.title: Present perfect continuous vs. present perfect simple
structures.content: The present perfect continuous emphasizes the duration of an action, while the present perfect simple emphasizes the completion of an action.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Future forms (using: present simple, present continuous, going to, will/won't)

structures.title: Future forms (using: present simple, present continuous, going to, will/won't)
structures.content: These structures are used to talk about future events. The present simple is used for scheduled events, the present continuous for planned events, 'going to' for intentions, and 'will/won't' for predictions and instant decisions.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: The passive (present simple, past simple, present continuous, present perfect)

structures.title: The passive (present simple, past simple, present continuous, present perfect)
structures.content: The passive voice is used when the focus is on the action rather than the doer of the action. It is formed using a form of 'to be' and the past participle.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Word formation (from 'root' word)

structures.title: Word formation (from 'root' word)
structures.content: This involves creating new words from a root word by adding prefixes and suffixes.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Comparative and superlative adjectives

structures.title: Comparative and superlative adjectives
structures.content: Comparative adjectives compare two things, and superlative adjectives compare three or more things.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Modal verbs to talk about rules and obligation in past and present: must, mustn't, have to, don't have to, had to, didn't have to

structures.title: Modal verbs to talk about rules and obligation in past and present: must, mustn't, have to, don't have to, had to, didn't have to
structures.content: These modal verbs are used to express obligation, necessity, and lack of necessity in the past and present.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Question tags to show interest / request clarification

structures.title: Question tags to show interest / request clarification
structures.content: Question tags are short questions added to the end of a statement to confirm information or show interest.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Present simple and present continuous (always with present continuous)

structures.title: Present simple and present continuous (always with present continuous)
structures.content: The present simple is used for habits and general truths, while the present continuous is used for actions happening now or around now.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Past simple vs. past continuous

structures.title: Past simple vs. past continuous
structures.content: The past simple is used for completed actions, and the past continuous is used for actions in progress at a specific time in the past.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: The passive (present and past simple)

structures.title: The passive (present and past simple)
structures.content: The passive voice is used when the focus is on the action rather than the doer of the action. It is formed using a form of 'to be' and the past participle.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Infinitive of purpose: She went to the shops to buy a new bag for school.

structures.title: Infinitive of purpose: She went to the shops to buy a new bag for school.
structures.content: The infinitive of purpose is used to express the reason for an action.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Future Simple (using shall); Future Perfect Simple; Future Perfect Continuous; Temporals (using: when, before, after, until, etc.)

structures.title: Future Simple (using shall)
structures.content: Example: I shall go to the market tomorrow.

structures.title: Future Perfect Simple
structures.content: Example: By next year, I shall have completed my studies.

structures.title: Future Perfect Continuous
structures.content: Example: By next month, I shall have been working here for two years.

structures.title: Temporals (using: when, before, after, until, etc.)
structures.content: Example: I shall finish my work before I go home.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Third Conditional and Mixed Conditionals

structures.title: Third Conditional
structures.content: Example: If I had known, I would have helped.

structures.title: Mixed Conditionals
structures.content: Example: If I were you, I would study harder.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Gerunds and Infinitives (using: make, let)

structures.title: Gerunds
structures.content: Example: I enjoy swimming.

structures.title: Infinitives (using: make, let)
structures.content: Example: I made him laugh.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Reported Speech: Commands and Questions

structures.title: Reported Speech: Commands
structures.content: Example: She told me to leave.

structures.title: Reported Speech: Questions
structures.content: Example: She asked me where I was going.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Modals (for requests, offers and suggestions, necessity, deduction, advice, criticism)

structures.title: Modals for Requests
structures.content: Example: Can you help me?

structures.title: Modals for Offers and Suggestions
structures.content: Example: Would you like some tea?

structures.title: Modals for Necessity
structures.content: Example: You must finish your homework.

structures.title: Modals for Deduction
structures.content: Example: She might be at home.

structures.title: Modals for Advice
structures.content: Example: You should see a doctor.

structures.title: Modals for Criticism
structures.content: Example: You ought to be more careful.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: The Passive: Impersonal and Personal Structures

structures.title: The Passive: Impersonal Structures
structures.content: Example: It is said that he is a good teacher.

structures.title: The Passive: Personal Structures
structures.content: Example: He was seen at the party.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Causative Forms (using: have or got)

structures.title: Causative Forms (using: have)
structures.content: Example: I had my car repaired.

structures.title: Causative Forms (using: got)
structures.content: Example: I got my hair cut.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Explaining Effects Using Determining Verbs (caused, led to)

structures.title: Explaining Effects Using Determining Verbs (caused)
structures.content: Example: The storm caused a lot of damage.

structures.title: Explaining Effects Using Determining Verbs (led to)
structures.content: Example: The accident led to a traffic jam.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Making Comparisons to Explain Opinion (for time using in the old days, in the past, nowadays, now)

structures.title: Making Comparisons to Explain Opinion (for time using in the old days)
structures.content: Example: In the old days, people lived simpler lives.

structures.title: Making Comparisons to Explain Opinion (for time using in the past)
structures.content: Example: In the past, people used to travel by horse.

structures.title: Making Comparisons to Explain Opinion (for time using nowadays)
structures.content: Example: Nowadays, people use computers for everything.

structures.title: Making Comparisons to Explain Opinion (for time using now)
structures.content: Example: Now, people communicate via the internet.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Using Conditional Sentences to Explain Reasons

structures.title: Using Conditional Sentences to Explain Reasons
structures.content: Example: If it rains, we will stay home.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Phrases to Show Opinion (for example: in my opinion)

structures.title: Phrases to Show Opinion (for example: in my opinion)
structures.content: Example: In my opinion, the movie was great.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Connecting Words Expressing a Contrast (using: although, however, on the other hand)

structures.title: Connecting Words Expressing a Contrast (using: although)
structures.content: Example: Although it was raining, we went out.

structures.title: Connecting Words Expressing a Contrast (using: however)
structures.content: Example: I like the book; however, it is quite expensive.

structures.title: Connecting Words Expressing a Contrast (using: on the other hand)
structures.content: Example: He is rich; on the other hand, he is not happy.
